summary: Adds three endpoints: a user search by name, a per-key request counter, and an upstream status probe. It also registers them in main.go.

findings.title: Search query built from request input
findings.problem: Search pastes the name query parameter straight into the SQL text with fmt.Sprintf. No placeholder or escaping protects the value.
findings.consequence: Any caller of GET /users can inject SQL to read or change any table the database user can reach.
findings.fix: Pass name to QueryContext as a bound parameter instead of formatting it into the query.
findings.suggested_change: rows, err := h.DB.QueryContext(r.Context(), "SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE name = ?", name)

findings.title: Mutex left locked on missing key
findings.problem: Count takes h.mu and then returns early when key is empty without unlocking it. The mutex stays locked for good.
findings.consequence: One request to GET /count without a key blocks every later Count request forever. Those goroutines pile up and the endpoint stops answering.
findings.fix: Check key before taking the lock, or unlock with defer right after Lock.

findings.title: Response body closed before error check
findings.problem: fetchStatus defers resp.Body.Close before it checks err. When http.Get fails, resp is nil, so the deferred call panics.
findings.consequence: Every request to GET /upstream panics while the upstream is unreachable. Clients get a dropped connection instead of the 502 answer.
findings.fix: Move the deferred Close below the err check.

findings.title: New handlers have no covering tests
findings.problem: The change adds Search, Count and Upstream, but the repository contains no test files. Nothing exercises the new error paths.
findings.consequence: Bugs like the stuck lock and the nil body panic reached review without any test catching them.
findings.fix: Add httptest-based tests for each new handler, including the missing key and failed upstream paths.

dropped.reason: This flags the same formatted query as c1. The c1 finding already covers that problem.
